standard_basis.performance_standards: IFC Performance Standards on Environmental and Social Sustainability, 1 January 2012 (in force)
standard_basis.revision_note: IFC is reviewing its Sustainability Framework. Phase I dialogue runs to December 2026 and public consultation on draft proposals starts in January 2027. Nothing has been approved and no effective date is set. The 2012 Performance Standards remain in force; draft provisions are not applied.
standard_basis.sustainability_policy: IFC Policy on Environmental and Social Sustainability, 1 January 2012 (paragraphs 19–44 used for the Exclusion List, due diligence, FIs and categories)
standard_basis.fi_guidance: IFC Guidance Note on Financial Intermediaries, 29 September 2023 (replaces the Interpretation Note on FIs of November 2018)
standard_basis.category_basis: The meaning of Categories A, B, C and FI-1 to FI-3 follows Sustainability Policy para 40 (and para 44 for FIs). The sector risk classes, the question-to-category rules, the sanity checks and the minimum-answers rule are EMC judgement: the Policy gives no sector list and no scoring rule.
standard_basis.cite_format: PSn para x = Performance Standard n, paragraph x. GNn-m = Guidance Note n, note m. Sustainability Policy para x. FI Guidance Note para x. fn = footnote. Question basis: PS = follows Performance Standard text; EMC = EMC practice or judgement.

status_rule.description: Per standard: any Yes triggers; every question answered No clears; no answers at all is Not screened; anything else (Not sure, or a mix of No and unanswered) is Needs review. PS1 is always triggered.

standards.name: Assessment and management of environmental and social risks and impacts
sections: Environmental and Social Assessment and Management System

base_actions.text: Adopt an environmental and social policy endorsed by senior management.
Identify risks and impacts through an assessment scaled to the project’s category.
Set up an ESMS: management programmes, organisational capacity and training, emergency preparedness, monitoring and review.
Run stakeholder engagement and an external grievance mechanism, with disclosure of relevant information.

Where gaps against the Performance Standards are found, agree an Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) with the investor; IFC makes it a condition of investment and expects the requirements to be met within a reasonable period. Category C projects often have no ESAP.
base_actions.cite: PS1 para 16; Sustainability Policy paras 22, 28 and fn 10

A.text: Commission a full ESIA prepared by competent professionals, with external experts for significant or technically complex issues, and run informed consultation and participation with affected communities. Where the impacts on communities are significant (or there are adverse impacts on Indigenous Peoples), IFC as investor judges whether this leads to Broad Community Support.

B.text: Commission a focused E&S assessment and an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP).

FI.text: Develop and operate an FI-level ESMS that fits the risk of the portfolio, incorporating the relevant principles of PS1: E&S policy, organisational capacity, risk identification and due diligence of each transaction, management programmes, monitoring and review, an external communications mechanism and emergency preparedness. FI-3 clients need only a simple screening procedure.
FI.cite: Sustainability Policy para 35; FI Guidance Note paras 6, 17, 23 and fn 20

FI.text: Screen every sub-project against the IFC Exclusion List and national law. FIs that serve only individual retail clients (mortgages, student loans) are generally not required to.
FI.cite: Sustainability Policy para 35; FI Guidance Note paras 7, 34 and fn 8, 10, 31

FI.text: Apply the relevant parts of PS2 to the FI’s own employees, and manage life and fire safety in premises open to the public. PS2 paras 7, 11, 12, 27, 28 and 29 are unlikely to apply to an FI.
FI.cite: Sustainability Policy para 35; FI Guidance Note para 18

FI.text: For FI-1, and for FI-2 that supports Higher Risk Transactions, apply the relevant Performance Standards to those sub-projects. They are equity, project finance or corporate finance over 36 months for activities involving resettlement, impacts on Indigenous Peoples, significant environmental, community, biodiversity or heritage impacts, significant retrenchment, or significant occupational health and safety risk.
FI.cite: Sustainability Policy para 35; FI Guidance Note paras 9, 34–35

FI.text: Confirm the scope of application: a specified end use of IFC funds covers that asset class only (and the same asset class when the FI also finances it from its own account); equity or general-purpose funding covers the whole portfolio originated from the date of IFC’s investment. The existing portfolio is not covered.
FI.cite: Sustainability Policy paras 36–37; FI Guidance Note paras 3–4 and fn 5

FI.text: Where IFC is the investor: report E&S performance to IFC each year (not FI-3), publish a summary of the ESMS, and (FI-1 and FI-2) notify IFC promptly of serious incidents at borrowers or investees. Private equity funds also disclose the sub-projects supported with IFC funding other than Category C.

Expect restrictions beyond the Exclusion List, for example coal-related sub-projects where the use of proceeds is defined (and trade finance for thermal coal); for funds, coal investments are excluded up front or IFC opts out.
FI.cite: FI Guidance Note para 7 and fn 11

standards.name: Labour and working conditions
sections: Working Conditions and Terms of Employment

base_actions.text: Adopt an HR policy and written terms of employment that meet national law and PS2.
Ensure no child labour, forced labour or discrimination, and respect workers’ freedom of association where national law allows it.
Set up a worker grievance mechanism, extended to contractor workers where the contractor has none.
Run an occupational health and safety programme: hazard identification, training, PPE and incident reporting.

documents: Contractor management procedure with PS2 clauses
Supply chain labour risk review (if high risk)

standards.name: Resource efficiency and pollution prevention

base_actions.text: Follow the World Bank Group EHS Guidelines (General and sector-specific), applying whichever is more stringent of the Guidelines and national standards.
Adopt resource efficiency measures for energy, water and materials that are technically and financially feasible and cost-effective.

documents: Pollution prevention and waste management plan

standards.name: Community health, safety and security
sections: Infrastructure and Equipment Design and Safety

base_actions.text: Assess risks to community health, safety and security and include controls in the ESMS.
Share emergency response arrangements with affected communities and local authorities, and help them take part.

documents: Community health, safety and security plan
Emergency response plan shared with communities
Security risk assessment and management plan
Labour influx management plan (communicable disease; GBV/SEA controls are lender practice)
Structural safety plan and external expert review (dams, tailings dams, ash ponds in high-risk locations)

standards.name: Land acquisition and involuntary resettlement
sections: Compensation and Benefits for Displaced Persons
Resettlement and Livelihood Restoration Planning and Implementation
Private Sector Responsibilities Under Government-Managed Resettlement

base_actions.text: Avoid or minimise displacement by considering alternative project designs and sites.

Compensate for lost assets at full replacement cost and restore livelihoods. People with no legal right or recognisable claim to the land are not paid for the land, but are offered resettlement with security of tenure and compensation for non-land assets owned before the cut-off date.
Set up a grievance mechanism for land issues early, before acquisition starts, and run a census with a published cut-off date.

standards.name: Biodiversity conservation and sustainable management of living natural resources
sections: Legally Protected and Internationally Recognized Areas
Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources

base_actions.text: Establish a biodiversity baseline and assess impacts on habitats and ecosystem services.
Apply the mitigation hierarchy: avoid, minimise, restore, then offset.

documents: Biodiversity Management Plan or Biodiversity Action Plan

standards.name: Indigenous Peoples
sections: Circumstances Requiring Free, Prior, and Informed Consent
Private Sector Responsibilities Where Government is Responsible for Managing Indigenous Peoples Issues

base_actions.text: Engage affected Indigenous communities through culturally appropriate informed consultation and participation, involving their representative bodies.
Prepare an Indigenous Peoples Plan, or a broader community development plan with separate components for Indigenous Peoples, with culturally appropriate benefits.

documents: Indigenous Peoples screening and social assessment
Indigenous Peoples Plan or Community Development Plan
Documented FPIC process and agreement (if required)

standards.name: Cultural heritage
sections: Protection of Cultural Heritage in Project Design and Execution

base_actions.text: Site and design the project to avoid significant adverse impacts on cultural heritage, and consult the communities who use it.
Where there is a chance of impacts, retain competent professionals to identify and protect cultural heritage.

documents: Cultural heritage screening or impact assessment
Chance-find procedure (where heritage is expected to be found)
standards.note_if_clear: Good practice, not a PS8 requirement unless heritage is expected to be found: where earthworks are planned, a chance-find clause in construction contracts is cheap insurance (PS8 para 8).

sectors.label: Solar power
sectors.exposure: PS3 low; PS5 and PS6 often decisive (land, grazing, birds, grassland); PS4 for lines and traffic

sectors.label: Wind power
sectors.exposure: PS6 birds and bats; PS5 land and access roads; PS4 blade throw, shadow flicker, traffic; PS7 where on tribal land

sectors.label: Hydropower or dams
sectors.exposure: High across PS4 (dam safety), PS5, PS6 (river), PS7, PS8; cumulative impacts

sectors.label: Power transmission and distribution
sectors.exposure: PS5 right-of-way; PS6 birds and forest corridors; PS4 line safety

policy_note.text: If the project involves the retail distribution of water, electricity, piped gas or telecommunications to the general public under monopoly conditions, IFC encourages public disclosure of household tariffs and tariff adjustment mechanisms, service standards, investment obligations and any ongoing government support.

sectors.label: Thermal power
sectors.exposure: PS3 high (emissions, GHG, ash, hazardous materials); PS4 including ash ponds

sectors.label: Roads, rail or metro
sectors.exposure: PS4 traffic and influx; PS5 right-of-way; PS6 for forest and coastal alignments

sectors.label: Ports or airports
sectors.exposure: PS5, PS6 coastal habitat, PS4 traffic and hazardous materials

sectors.label: Oil, gas or pipelines
sectors.exposure: PS3, PS4 (pipeline safety), PS5 right-of-way, PS6

policy_note.text: Where IFC invests, it assesses the governance risks to the expected benefits of an oil, gas or mining project and does not support the project if the risks outweigh the benefits. The client must publicly disclose material project payments to the host government (royalties, taxes, profit sharing). The principal contract with government, and any significant amendments, must be public, with commercially sensitive information redacted; a published summary of key terms may be accepted instead.

sectors.label: Mining or quarrying
sectors.exposure: High across PS3 to PS8; tailings safety; legacy land

policy_note.text: Where IFC invests, it assesses the governance risks to the expected benefits of an oil, gas or mining project and does not support the project if the risks outweigh the benefits. The client must publicly disclose material project payments to the host government (royalties, taxes, profit sharing). The principal contract with government, and any significant amendments, must be public, with commercially sensitive information redacted; a published summary of key terms may be accepted instead.

sectors.label: Heavy industry (cement, steel, chemicals)
sectors.exposure: PS3 high; PS4 hazardous materials; PS2 OHS

sectors.label: Light manufacturing
sectors.exposure: PS2 and PS3 moderate; PS2 supply chain in textiles and electronics

sectors.label: Agribusiness or food processing
sectors.exposure: PS2 seasonal and child labour; PS3 pesticides; PS6 sourcing

sectors.label: Forestry or plantations
sectors.exposure: PS6 habitat conversion; PS7 customary use; PS2

sectors.label: Real estate, hospitality or commercial buildings
sectors.exposure: PS2 construction labour; PS4 life and fire safety; PS5 if land assembled

sectors.label: Water, sanitation or waste
sectors.exposure: PS3 effluent and sludge; PS4; PS5 for pipelines and plants

policy_note.text: If the project involves the retail distribution of water, electricity, piped gas or telecommunications to the general public under monopoly conditions, IFC encourages public disclosure of household tariffs and tariff adjustment mechanisms, service standards, investment obligations and any ongoing government support.

sectors.label: Healthcare or education
sectors.exposure: PS1 and PS2; healthcare adds PS3 medical waste (so pollution answers block Category C here)

sectors.label: Financial intermediary (bank, NBFC, fund, insurer)
sectors.exposure: Apply through the FI’s ESMS to sub-projects

questions.text: Will the project employ workers, directly or through contractors, during construction or operation?
questions.if_yes_reason: The project has a workforce, direct or contracted.
questions.if_open_confirm: Confirm workforce numbers for construction and operation.

questions.text: Will a large share of the work be done by contractors, subcontractors or migrant workers?
questions.if_yes_reason: A large contracted or migrant workforce.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get the contracting strategy and expected contractor headcount.

actions_if_yes.text: Write PS2 requirements into contracts and monitor contractors’ labour and safety performance.
Check recruitment fees, wage payment and retention of identity documents for migrant workers; workers must keep their own passports and documents.

questions.text: Will workers live in camps or project-provided accommodation?
questions.section: Working Conditions and Terms of Employment
questions.if_yes_reason: Worker accommodation will be provided.
questions.if_open_confirm: Ask whether labour camps are planned, and for how many workers.

actions_if_yes.text: Build and run camps to the IFC/EBRD Workers’ Accommodation guidance: space, sanitation, water, fire safety and privacy; monitor conditions.

questions.text: Do primary suppliers come from sectors with known forced labour, child labour or serious safety risks (for example polysilicon, cotton, bricks, mica, seafood)?
questions.if_yes_reason: The primary supply chain carries labour risk.
questions.if_open_confirm: List the main materials and where primary suppliers source them.

actions_if_yes.text: Map primary suppliers and review the risk of child labour, forced labour and serious safety issues; require remediation, or shift to other suppliers over time, where it is found.

questions.text: Are layoffs or collective retrenchment planned, for example after an acquisition or restructuring?
questions.if_yes_reason: Collective retrenchment is planned.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check restructuring plans and post-acquisition staffing.

actions_if_yes.text: Prepare a retrenchment plan: alternatives analysis, consultation with workers and their organisations, notice and severance, and non-discriminatory selection.

questions.text: Will the project release air emissions, wastewater or waste, or use or store hazardous materials?
questions.if_yes_reason: Emissions, effluent, waste or hazardous materials are involved.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get a process description listing emissions, effluents and wastes.

actions_if_yes.text: Set up waste and hazardous materials management, and monitor emissions and effluents against permit and EHS Guideline limits.

questions.text: Will the project draw significant amounts of water, or is it in a water-stressed area?
questions.if_yes_reason: Significant water use or a water-stressed location.
questions.if_open_confirm: Find the water source, expected demand and local water stress.

actions_if_yes.text: Assess water availability and effects on other users; adopt water efficiency and reuse measures.

questions.text: Are direct emissions plus emissions from purchased energy likely to exceed 25,000 tonnes CO₂-equivalent a year?
questions.if_yes_reason: GHG emissions above 25,000 tCO₂e a year.
questions.if_open_confirm: Estimate annual fuel and electricity use to test the 25,000 tCO₂e threshold.

actions_if_yes.text: Quantify direct emissions and emissions from purchased energy annually, and consider cost-effective options to reduce them.

questions.text: Will pesticides or other agrochemicals be used?
questions.if_yes_reason: Pesticides or agrochemicals will be used.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check pest and vegetation control practices.

actions_if_yes.text: Adopt integrated pest management. Do not purchase, store, use, manufacture or trade WHO Class Ia or Ib pesticides; Class II only with appropriate controls and trained handlers. Pesticides and herbicides that are illegal or internationally banned are on the IFC Exclusion List.

questions.text: Do communities live close to the site or along its access roads?
questions.if_yes_reason: Communities live near the site or its access routes.
questions.if_open_confirm: Map settlements around the site and along access routes.

actions_if_yes.text: Assess community exposure to dust, noise, water contamination and disease, and set controls.

questions.text: Will heavy vehicles use public roads, or will hazardous materials be transported?
questions.if_yes_reason: Heavy traffic or hazardous materials on public roads.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get the construction logistics plan and expected vehicle movements.

actions_if_yes.text: Prepare a traffic and road safety plan; train drivers and manage routes near schools and villages; control the safety of hazardous materials deliveries.

questions.text: Does the project include structures or buildings the public will use, or whose failure could endanger the public (tanks, pipelines, transmission lines, bridges, tall buildings)? Dams, tailings dams and ash ponds are asked separately.
questions.section: Infrastructure and Equipment Design and Safety
questions.if_yes_reason: Structures that could endanger the public if they fail, or that the public will use.
questions.if_open_confirm: Identify structural elements whose failure could affect the public.

actions_if_yes.text: Have competent professionals design and build structures to good international industry practice, certified or approved by competent authorities or professionals; consider fire, life safety and universal access for buildings the public uses.
Prepare emergency response plans jointly with local authorities and communities.

questions.text: Does the project include a dam, tailings dam or ash pond in a location where its failure could threaten communities (settlements downstream, steep terrain, seismic zone)?
questions.section: Infrastructure and Equipment Design and Safety
questions.if_yes_reason: A dam, tailings dam or ash pond whose failure could threaten communities.
questions.if_open_confirm: Ask the design engineer whether any dam, tailings dam or ash pond is planned and who lives downstream.

actions_if_yes.text: Engage external experts, separate from the designers and builders, to review the structure from early development through design, construction, operation and decommissioning.

questions.text: Will private security guards or public security forces protect the site?
questions.if_yes_reason: Security personnel will be used.
questions.if_open_confirm: Ask whether guards or police will be deployed at site.

actions_if_yes.text: Assess security risks; make reasonable inquiries that guards are not implicated in past abuses; train them in use of force and conduct toward workers and communities; allow force only for preventive and defensive purposes in proportion to the threat. For public security forces, assess and document the risks. Provide a grievance mechanism for communities. (The Voluntary Principles on Security and Human Rights are a common benchmark; the Performance Standard text does not name them.)

questions.text: Will many outside workers arrive compared with the local population?
questions.if_yes_reason: A large labour influx is expected.
questions.if_open_confirm: Compare peak workforce with the population of nearby villages.

actions_if_yes.text: Manage the communicable disease risk that comes with labour influx (health screening, awareness programmes with host communities).
Lender practice, not PS4 text: add a worker code of conduct, a community grievance channel, and controls on gender-based violence and sexual exploitation.

questions.text: Does the project need land that is not already built-up premises leased on the open market: new land, a purchase, a long lease, a right-of-way or an easement?
questions.if_yes_reason: New land, right-of-way or lease is needed. PS5 applies unless every parcel is a genuinely voluntary transaction (PS5 para 6), which has to be shown.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get the land schedule: area, ownership and how each parcel is being secured.

actions_if_yes.text: Show, parcel by parcel, that each transaction was voluntary (the seller was not obliged to sell and the buyer could not have used expropriation). Where it was not, or where people used the land, PS5 applies in full.

questions.text: Do people live on, farm, graze or collect resources from that land, including government or ‘vacant’ land?
questions.if_yes_reason: People use the land, formally or informally.
questions.if_open_confirm: Commission a land-use and livelihood survey. ‘Vacant’ government land does not by itself rule out PS5.

actions_if_yes.text: Run a census and socio-economic survey with a published cut-off date, covering informal users. Those with no legal claim are not paid for the land but receive compensation for non-land assets and help to restore livelihoods.
Prepare a Livelihood Restoration Plan for economic displacement.

questions.text: Will any households have to move their homes or structures?
questions.if_yes_reason: Households will be physically displaced.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check whether any dwellings or structures fall within the footprint or right-of-way.

actions_if_yes.text: Prepare a Resettlement Action Plan with replacement housing or cash at full replacement cost, security of tenure, and transition support.

questions.text: Is the loss of land or land access likely to affect many people, whole communities, or the main livelihood of many users?
questions.if_yes_reason: Land loss or restricted access could affect many people or their main livelihoods.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get the land-use survey or at least a count of households that farm, graze or collect resources on the land.

actions_if_yes.text: Size the livelihood impacts early and treat the Livelihood Restoration Plan as a major workstream, with independent monitoring and a completion audit.

questions.text: Is the government acquiring the land, or could it expropriate if negotiations fail?
questions.section: Private Sector Responsibilities Under Government-Managed Resettlement
questions.if_yes_reason: Government acquisition or expropriation is involved.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check whether land is acquired under acquisition law, or by negotiation backed by expropriation powers.

actions_if_yes.text: Treat the acquisition as involuntary; identify the government’s resettlement measures and, where they fall short of PS5, prepare a supplemental plan with top-up compensation where needed.

questions.text: Will people lose access to grazing land, forests, fishing grounds or other natural resources?
questions.if_yes_reason: Access to land or natural resources will be restricted.
questions.if_open_confirm: Identify community use of resources in and around the footprint.

actions_if_yes.text: Agree measures for access restriction and alternative livelihoods with the affected users.

questions.text: Was land for this project acquired earlier by the government or a previous owner?
questions.section: Private Sector Responsibilities Under Government-Managed Resettlement
questions.if_yes_reason: Land was acquired earlier by a third party.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get records of earlier acquisition, compensation paid and outstanding grievances.

actions_if_yes.text: Carry out a legacy land audit and agree a corrective action plan for any gaps against PS5. (Lenders expect this because the project inherits third-party risks; PS1 requires the client to address them as far as it can.)

questions.text: Is the site within or near a legally protected area or an internationally recognised area (UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site, Man and the Biosphere reserve, Key Biodiversity Area, Ramsar wetland), or an eco-sensitive zone? About 10 km is a screening distance, not a PS rule.
questions.section: Legally Protected and Internationally Recognized Areas
questions.if_yes_reason: Near a protected or internationally recognised area.
questions.if_open_confirm: Run an IBAT or equivalent proximity screen.

actions_if_yes.text: Demonstrate the project is legally permitted, follow the area’s management plan, consult its managers and communities, and add programmes that support the area’s conservation aims.

questions.text: Will the project clear or alter natural habitat (forest, grassland, wetland, river, mangrove, coast)?
questions.if_yes_reason: Natural habitat will be converted or altered.
questions.if_open_confirm: Commission a habitat map of the footprint.

actions_if_yes.text: Do not significantly convert or degrade natural habitat unless the conditions in para 14 are met; design mitigation for no net loss of biodiversity.

questions.text: Could the site hold critical habitat: habitat that matters for Critically Endangered or Endangered species, endemic or restricted-range species, large concentrations of migratory or congregatory species (flyways, stopovers), or highly threatened ecosystems? Examples: Great Indian Bustard, vultures, elephant corridors.
questions.if_yes_reason: The site may hold critical habitat (threatened, endemic or migratory species).
questions.if_open_confirm: Ask a specialist ecologist for a species presence check that looks beyond notified protected areas.

actions_if_yes.text: Carry out a Critical Habitat Assessment; the habitat often extends beyond notified boundaries.

Where critical habitat is confirmed, show there is no viable alternative on non-critical habitat, no measurable adverse impact on the qualifying biodiversity values, no net reduction of any Critically Endangered or Endangered species population, and a long-term monitoring programme; then describe the mitigation in a Biodiversity Action Plan designed for net gains.

questions.text: Does the project produce or buy living natural resources (crops, timber, palm oil, fish, aquaculture)?
questions.section: Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources
questions.if_yes_reason: Production or sourcing of living natural resources.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check whether the project produces or buys agricultural, forestry or fishery products.

actions_if_yes.text: Apply credible sustainability standards to production, and check primary suppliers are not converting natural or critical habitat.

questions.text: Do local communities depend on ecosystems the project could affect (water, fuelwood, fisheries, flood protection)?
questions.if_yes_reason: Communities depend on ecosystem services the project could affect.
questions.if_open_confirm: Identify ecosystem services used by nearby communities.

actions_if_yes.text: Assess priority ecosystem services and maintain their value and function for affected communities.

questions.text: Are Indigenous Peoples present in or using the project area (in India, Scheduled Tribes or Adivasi communities, or a Fifth or Sixth Schedule area)?
questions.if_yes_reason: Indigenous Peoples are present in the area of influence.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check the Scheduled Area status of affected villages and census data on Scheduled Tribe population.

actions_if_yes.text: Screen and assess impacts on Indigenous Peoples through a social assessment by qualified specialists; take advice on whether a group counts as Indigenous Peoples for PS7.

questions.text: Will the project be on, or take natural resources from, land that Indigenous Peoples traditionally own or customarily use; relocate them from such land; or significantly affect cultural heritage that is critical to them?
questions.section: Circumstances Requiring Free, Prior, and Informed Consent
questions.if_yes_reason: Circumstances that require Free, Prior and Informed Consent.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check customary claims, forest rights titles and community use of the footprint.

actions_if_yes.text: Obtain and document Free, Prior and Informed Consent through good-faith negotiation with the affected communities, supported by an independent expert as needed. IFC as investor reviews the consent process in depth.

questions.text: Are there known heritage sites near the footprint (protected monuments, temples, sacred groves, graves, shrines)?
questions.section: Protection of Cultural Heritage in Project Design and Execution
questions.if_yes_reason: Known cultural heritage near the site.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check national and state protected monument lists, and ask communities about sacred places.

actions_if_yes.text: Retain competent professionals, consult the communities that use the site, and keep community access to it.

questions.text: Could the project significantly damage or remove cultural heritage that cannot be replaced, or that is internationally or nationally important (a World Heritage property, an ancient monument, a major sacred site)?
questions.if_yes_reason: Critical cultural heritage could be significantly affected.
questions.if_open_confirm: Ask a heritage specialist whether any footprint or access route touches a nationally or internationally important heritage site.

actions_if_yes.text: Do not remove, significantly alter or damage critical cultural heritage. Where that is unavoidable in exceptional circumstances, run informed consultation and participation with a good-faith negotiation and a documented outcome, and retain external experts.

questions.text: Will there be significant excavation or earthworks in an area where cultural heritage is likely to be found?
questions.if_yes_reason: Ground disturbance in an area where cultural heritage is expected to be found.
questions.if_open_confirm: Get the earthworks plan and an archaeological potential screen.

actions_if_yes.text: Have qualified specialists screen archaeological potential before earthworks start, and put a chance-find procedure into the ESMS: work stops at a find until competent professionals assess it.

questions.text: Will the project use cultural heritage or traditional knowledge for commercial purposes?
questions.if_yes_reason: Commercial use of cultural heritage.
questions.if_open_confirm: Check whether heritage sites or traditional knowledge are part of the business model.

actions_if_yes.text: Inform the communities of their rights, the scope of the commercial use and its consequences; do not proceed without informed consultation and participation (good-faith negotiation, documented outcome) and fair, equitable benefit sharing. For Indigenous Peoples’ heritage, Free, Prior and Informed Consent applies and PS7 governs.

category_rules.description: Evaluated in order; the first rule that matches wins. The category is provisional. The meaning of each category follows the IFC Sustainability Policy (2012) paragraphs 40–44. The rules that turn checklist answers into a category are EMC judgement: the Policy defines the categories in words and does not prescribe them.

order.label: Financial intermediary
order.why: Investment through a financial intermediary. IFC sets FI-1, FI-2 or FI-3 from the exposure of the portfolio (type, size, sector, tenor), which this checklist does not collect (Sustainability Policy paras 40, 44). The FI applies the Exclusion List and national law to sub-projects and runs an ESMS that fits the risk of its portfolio. To screen a sub-project, answer the questions for a typical higher-risk one: the standards then show what it would trigger. PS2 also applies to the FI’s own staff (FI Guidance Note para 18).

order.label: Provisional Category A
order.why: Potentially significant adverse risks or impacts that are diverse, irreversible or unprecedented (Sustainability Policy para 40). Expect a full ESIA.

order.label: Not yet categorised
order.why: Choose a sector and answer at least 10 questions with Yes or No to get a provisional category.

order.label: Provisional Category C
order.why: Minimal or no adverse risks or impacts on current answers (Sustainability Policy para 40).
order.note_if_any_open: Questions that could move this to B are still open or marked Not sure.

order.label: Provisional Category B
order.why: Potentially limited adverse risks or impacts: few in number, generally site-specific, largely reversible and readily addressed through mitigation (Sustainability Policy para 40). A focused assessment and ESMP are expected.

a_signals.description: Every question with a_signal true adds its if_yes_reason when answered Yes.

a_signals.reason: High-risk sector on a greenfield site.
a_signals.basis: EMC judgement. Sustainability Policy paras 42–43 require the inherent risk of the sector and the setting to be weighed when the footprint is not yet known; they do not name sectors or say a greenfield site is Category A.

a_signals.reason: Natural habitat altered near a protected or internationally recognised area.
Commercial use of Indigenous Peoples’ cultural heritage requires Free, Prior and Informed Consent (PS7 para 17).

watch.description: For B or C: every question with a_signal true that is not answered No becomes a ‘could move to A’ item, using its if_open_confirm text.

sanity_checks.message: Solar, wind and transmission projects nearly always need land or a right-of-way. Check the No on the land question.
Hydropower normally includes a dam or weir. Check the No on the dam question.
This type of project nearly always needs land or a right-of-way. Check the No on the land question.
This sector releases emissions, effluent or waste. Check the No on the pollution question.
Thermal power is very likely to exceed 25,000 tCO₂e a year. Check the No on the GHG question.
Coal-based thermal plants normally have an ash pond. Check the No on the dam, tailings or ash pond question.
Most mines have a tailings or waste storage facility. Check the No on the dam, tailings or ash pond question.
Mines, plantations and dams almost always alter natural habitat. Check the No on the habitat question.
Agribusiness and forestry produce or buy living natural resources. Check the No on that question.
Most agricultural operations use some agrochemicals. Check the No on the pesticide question.

exclusion_list.name: IFC Exclusion List (2007), as amended 8 December 2025
exclusion_list.source: https://www.ifc.org/exclusionlist (text supplied by EMC, 29 October 2026). Applies to transactions and engagements mandated after 31 December 2025.
exclusion_list.cite: Sustainability Policy para 19; IFC Exclusion List
exclusion_list.prompt: Before relying on this result, confirm the project does not involve an activity on the IFC Exclusion List. IFC does not finance such projects, whatever the Performance Standards result.
exclusion_list.fi_prompt: For a financial intermediary the list applies to the sub-projects it finances, with extra exclusions for FIs (forced and harmful child labour; commercial logging in primary tropical moist forest; wood and forestry products not from sustainably managed forests). Microfinance and trade finance have shorter lists.
exclusion_list.intro: IFC does not finance the following projects:

items.text: Production or trade in any product or activity deemed illegal under host country laws or regulations or international conventions and agreements, or subject to international bans, such as pharmaceuticals, pesticides/herbicides, ozone depleting substances, PCB’s, wildlife or products regulated under CITES.
Production or trade in weapons and munitions.
Production or trade in alcoholic beverages (excluding beer and wine).
Production or trade in unbonded asbestos fibers. This does not apply to purchase and use of bonded asbestos cement sheeting where the asbestos content is less than 20%.
Drift net fishing in the marine environment using nets in excess of 2.5 km. in length.

footnotes.1: This does not apply to project sponsors who are not substantially involved in these activities. “Not substantially involved” means that the activity concerned is ancillary to a project sponsor’s primary operations.
footnotes.2: Forced labor means all work or service, not voluntarily performed, that is extracted from an individual under threat of force or penalty.
footnotes.3: Harmful child labor means the employment of children that is economically exploitive, or is likely to be hazardous to, or to interfere with, the child’s education, or to be harmful to the child’s health, or physical, mental, spiritual, moral, or social development.

exclusion_list.reasonableness_test: A reasonableness test will be applied when the activities of the project company would have a significant development impact but circumstances of the country require adjustment to the Exclusion List.

general.label: All financial intermediaries, except microfinance and trade finance below, apply these in addition to the Exclusion List

items.text: Production or activities involving harmful or exploitative forms of forced labor/harmful child labor.
Commercial logging operations for use in primary tropical moist forest.
Production or trade in wood or other forestry products other than from sustainably managed forests.

microfinance.label: When investing in microfinance activities, FIs apply these in addition to the Exclusion List

items.text: Production or activities involving harmful or exploitative forms of forced labor/harmful child labor.

Production, trade, storage, or transport of significant volumes of hazardous chemicals, or commercial scale usage of hazardous chemicals. Hazardous chemicals include gasoline, kerosene, and other petroleum products.
Production or activities that impinge on the lands owned, or claimed under adjudication, by Indigenous Peoples, without full documented consent of such peoples.

trade_finance.label: For trade finance projects, FIs apply this in addition to the Exclusion List

items.text: Production or activities involving harmful or exploitative forms of forced labor/harmful child labor.

exclusion_list.fi_substantially_involved: For an FI, “substantially involved” (footnote 1) is generally taken to mean a cumulative portfolio exposure above 5 percent to investees or borrowers that earn more than 20 percent of their revenues from an excluded activity (for multi-seller e-commerce platforms, a gross merchandise value indicator replaces the revenue test). The 5 percent threshold would not generally apply to private equity funds. FIs that serve only individual retail clients (mortgages, student loans) are generally not required to apply the Exclusion List.
exclusion_list.fi_cite: FI Guidance Note para 7 and fn 8–10, 31
exclusion_list.amendment_note: The list was amended on 8 December 2025 to remove ‘production or trade in radioactive materials’. An older copy that still lists radioactive materials is out of date.
exclusion_list.other_restrictions_note: IFC may also restrict activities beyond this list in a project’s legal documents. For FI projects with a defined use of proceeds it excludes coal-related sub-projects (coal mining, coal transport, coal-fired power plants and infrastructure dedicated to them) and trade finance for thermal coal (FI Guidance Note para 7 and fn 11).

by_ps.1: The EIA Notification 2006 requires prior Environmental Clearance only for listed project categories. Projects outside the list still need an IFC PS-aligned assessment if the financing applies the Performance Standards.
by_ps.2: The four Labour Codes (in force from 21 November 2025) and state rules cover wages, social security and safety. PS2 adds oversight of contractor and supply chain labour, a worker grievance mechanism for all workers, and a fair retrenchment process.
by_ps.3: Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate from the State Pollution Control Board and the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules 2016 cover pollution control. PS3 adds the EHS Guidelines (the more stringent applies), resource efficiency and annual GHG quantification above 25,000 tCO₂e.
by_ps.4: Indian law has no general requirement to assess community health and safety outside hazardous-industry rules; the Dam Safety Act 2021 covers specified dams. Expectations on security personnel conduct and on external review of high-risk dams and tailings dams come mainly from PS4.
by_ps.5: RFCTLARR 2013 governs government acquisition but not private negotiated purchase, and gives limited cover to informal users. PS5 applies to negotiated purchases only where expropriation was the fallback, and covers informal users and economic displacement.
by_ps.6: The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, the Biological Diversity Act 2002, the forest conservation law (now the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam 1980) and eco-sensitive zone notifications protect designated areas. The PS6 critical habitat test has no direct Indian equivalent.
by_ps.7: Fifth and Sixth Schedule provisions, PESA 1996 and the Forest Rights Act 2006 give gram sabhas consultation and consent roles. PS7 applies in wider circumstances, and FPIC must be documented.
by_ps.8: The AMASR Act 1958 sets prohibited (100 m) and regulated (200 m) zones around centrally protected monuments. Community and intangible heritage is covered mainly by PS8.

IN.ec_gate_note: This sector is not listed in the schedule of India’s EIA Notification 2006, so IFC PS, through the financier, may be the only framework requiring an E&S assessment.
